summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: Codified supermajority thresholds for constitutional revision (the fixed textual kernel) read as a sacred stabilization tool ensuring deep democratic consensus versus read as an anti-majoritarian veto-trap that entrenches minority rule and blocks necessary adaptation. The contest directly shapes institutional drift and alternative reachability.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The judicially created doctrine of qualified immunity (the shared legal kernel text/precedent) read by law enforcement as a vital protective scaffold against bad-faith personal liability versus read by civil rights advocates as an extractive shield that guarantees a police accountability vacuum. Each reading emits structurally opposite victim and beneficiary structures from an identical legal substrate[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: A permissive open-source license text (the shared kernel) read by the software commons as a coordination floor maximizing universal freedom of implementation versus read by corporate enterprise as an uncompensated extraction substrate to build closed-source product moats. This represents a live, present-day interpretation contest over copyright relaxation[cite: 2, 3].

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The traditional right of French Parlements to register and remonstrate royal edicts (the historical practice-norm kernel) read by regional magistrates as a fundamental constitutional check preserving the realm's unwritten laws versus read by the Crown as a minoritarian obstruction mechanism protecting elite tax exemptions. An authority-grounding contest that directly preceded structural collapse[cite: 2, 3].
